literal: Having known the nature, before a capable assembly, will not slip in speech, those of purity who have known the collection of words.
translation: Those of pure mind who know the arrangement of words will not falter in their speech before a powerful assembly, once they have understood its nature.
modern: அவையின் தன்மையை அறிந்து, சொற்களின் தொகுதியை உணர்ந்த தூய்மையான அறிவை உடையவர்கள், வல்லமை மிக்க அவையின் முன் பேசும்போது வாய் தவறிப் பிழை செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains how a speaker can address an audience without fear or error. Those who possess a pure, flawless intellect and a deep mastery over vocabulary ('colliṉ tokai') will never falter or make slips of the tongue ('vāy cōrār'). By first analyzing and understanding the specific nature of the audience ('vakai aṟintu'), they can confidently deliver their speech even before a highly capable and powerful assembly ('val avai').
